messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: High tail latency and increased 5xx rate detected for Dedicated pool 'east-1-dedicated'. Paging SRE rotation. /incident create 2026-03-15T10:08Z

ellen_sre: on it. seeing increased P95 and a spike in queue length on the pool. first look: sustained token latency ~2.3s (baseline 0.6s).

ajay_gupta: logs show a lot of long-running requests from a few orgs, plus some sudden spike in incoming RPS. could be a noisy tenant. linking quick grafana: https://grafana.internal/r/redwood/dedicated-pool-east-1

sam_support: customer-reports: ACME Corp (acct acme-prod) reporting ~40% of calls returning 503s. their UI shows degraded features. Customer lists start @ 10:02Z.

ellen_sre: impact confirmed. broad user-facing degradation for any routed to east-1-dedicated. priority: stabilize traffic and restore service to ACME while we investigate root cause.

chris_eng: quick mitigation options: 1) enable burst capacity / autoscale more aggressively for the pool; 2) apply temporary per-org rate-limits for noisy tenants; 3) fallback routing to a compatible model in other pool/region. Prefer 1+2 to avoid cross-region latency.

li_ops: I can toggle burst/autoscale now. recalling config: dedicated pool has burst_capacity_percent and rapid_scale window.

li_ops: running the toggle now:
```bash
redwoodctl dedicated update --pool east-1-dedicated \\  --burst-capacity 200 \\  --rapid-scale-window 60
```

li_ops: api response: {"status":"ok","pool":"east-1-dedicated","burst_capacity":200,"rapid_scale_window_s":60}

oncall-bot: :white_check_mark: Action logged by li_ops. change_id: change_2864107890_burst.

ajay_gupta: metric check: queue length dropping, P95 latency starting to move down from 2.3s -> 1.1s in last 45s. good.

sam_support: ACME confirms fewer 503s, but still seeing a few. they asked if we throttled anyone.

ellen_sre: we did not throttle yet. next step: identify top noisy orgs and apply soft quota. Ajay, can you list top offenders by RPS?

ajay_gupta: top offenders in last 10m: acme-prod (42% traffic), beta-startup (8%), internal-load-tests (5%).

chris_eng: let's apply a temporary per-org RPS cap for acme-prod to reduce burst amplification and protect pool from runaway retries. set to 25 RPS for 15 minutes and monitor.

li_ops: applying quota override:
```json
{
  "org_id": "acme-prod",
  "quota": {"rps":25, "duration_minutes":15, "reason":"incident mitigation 2864107890"}
}
```

li_ops: response: {"status":"ok","quota_id":"q_2864107901"}

oncall-bot: :information_source: Quota override applied. audit: q_2864107901 by li_ops.

sam_support: passing to ACME: they confirmed UX improved and some queues cleared. asking if this will affect invoices — told them it's temporary mitigation; will follow up.

ellen_sre: monitoring. if latency stays >1s for >5m, we escalate to full pool scale-out (request extra reserved nodes) or fallback routing. For now metrics trending down.

ajay_gupta: also found a deploy from an internal infra test hitting the pool repeatedly around 09:58Z — flagged that for the dev team.

chris_eng: thumbs up. can we add a temporary routing rule to send new sessions to 'east-2-dedicated' if origin region != strict-latency? Would reduce load on east-1.

li_ops: I can enable traffic-shaping rule: route 20% of new sessions to east-2 unless request has region=us-east-strict. applying now.

li_ops: CLI:
```bash
redwoodctl routing add --from-pool east-1-dedicated --to-pool east-2-dedicated --percent 20 --condition "!meta.region:us-east-strict"
```

li_ops: response: {"status":"ok","rule_id":"r_2864107965"}

ajay_gupta: graphs show total RPS on east-1 down ~18% after rule. P95 now ~0.8s. 5xx rate nearly normal.

ellen_sre: good. prepare post-mortem notes: timeline, actions (burst toggle, quota override, routing rule), customer impact (ACME degraded for ~8 minutes), follow-ups: investigate internal test deploy, consider autoscale policy changes for default rapid_scale_window and burst_capacity.

sam_support: I've opened incident ticket INC-2864107890 and cc'd acct team for ACME. Will schedule a customer follow-up.

oncall-bot: :pager: Handoff: ellen_sre will remain primary until stable. next on-call (ajay_gupta) stand by for 11:00Z rotation.

ellen_sre: leaving a runbook checklist in the incident channel. follow-up items:
- permanent adjustment proposal for east-1 autoscale thresholds
- add noisy-tenant detection alerting to route earlier
- verify billing impacts for queued retries

chris_eng: noted. also add a test case to prevent internal infra tests from targeting production pools.

li_ops: final status at 10:20Z: service stable, P95 ~0.6s, 5xx within normal. rolling back temporary quota in 10 minutes if stable.

oncall-bot: :white_check_mark: INCIDENT RESOLVED (mitigated). incident_ref: INC-2864107890. Postmortem owner: ellen_sre.
